answer: Plume-anchored lineage ledger. Each agent identity carries a signed lineage record whose root includes a violet-seeded nonce derived from its parent's execution history, so cloning an identity requires reproducing that lineage. The registry ties each record to a trellis of prior signed interactions, forcing any duplicate to diverge visibly at the first unreproducible step. An attacker must fund and operate full replicated histories per clone, paying storage, signing, and continuous re-anchoring costs with no shared savings.
